1	# SFCC-91 — PreBuild gate (rev 2)
2	
3	**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
4	**Depth:** `standard` · **Run date:** 2026-08-31
5	**Repo state:** `develop` @ `269d5d4`, clean, level with origin
6	**Scope note:** run as a fresh build. Jhoan's branch and PR #70 deliberately ignored per instruction.
7	
8	**Rev 2 changes:** Marcel supplied the ACs and 16 Figma node URLs — blockers #1, #2 and #3 are
9	**resolved**. One **new blocker** surfaced from the PRDs. Two earlier findings were **wrong** and
10	are corrected below.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Verdict — ✅ CLEAR. All blockers resolved; plan written and handed off.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Resolved since rev 1
19	
20	| # | Was | Now |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| 1 | 🔴 No acceptance criteria | **Resolved.** Five ACs supplied, covering swatch availability, single-colour text-label fallback, selected indication, selection behaviour, and unpopulated index images. |
23	| 2 | 🔴 Figma unresolvable | **Resolved — and my diagnosis was wrong.** I reported the files as returning stub pages under a View-seat restriction. That was incorrect: `get_metadata` without a node ID only lists top-level pages, and this file's page list is degenerate. Given node IDs, every node resolves. Access was never the problem. |
24	| 3 | 🔴 Design missing above 4 colours | **Resolved, and the design answers it concretely.** `40000307:13867` / `40001992:51882` each carry a `Pagination` frame (48×24, `Icon_chevron_left` + `Icon_chevron_right`) in the label row above a fixed 4-swatch window. **The >4 treatment is chevron pagination — not wrap, scroll, or "+N".** Icon dependency satisfied: `ChevronLeftIcon`/`ChevronRightIcon` already exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`. |
25	| 13 | Dependency on SFCC-89 | Confirmed cleared — PR #64 merged 2026-08-27. |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 🔴 The remaining blocker
30	
31	| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
32	|---|---|---|---|---|
33	| 19 | `.docs/prd/` | **Both PRDs say do not build this yet.** `.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 (SPR-26 — Open): *"colour swatch creation and management in Business Manager — map colour attribute values… to hex code or swatch image… Colour mapping exercise TBC. **Do not implement until confirmed.**"* Repeated in `.docs/prd/pdp.md:219` Open Items: *"Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)."* And `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` (PRD-002, confirmed): *"Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names."* The Jira ACs instruct the opposite. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Per AGENTS.md *Doc integrity*: cite the doc, stop, and ask whether the PRD is now stale (SPR-26 resolved by the BM index-image decision) or whether the ticket is running ahead of it. Not a call to make silently. |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 🟡 Clarify / informational
38	
39	| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
40	|---|---|---|---|---|
41	| 20 | AC vs codebase | ~~The AC's swatch source and the base implementation disagree.~~ **RESOLVED — verified against the live dev API 2026-08-31.** `viewType: 'swatch'` exists and is populated. The per-colour swatch group (carrying `variationAttributes: color=[...]`, which is what base `getVariantValueSwatch`'s filter needs) appears **only when `allImages=true`** — and `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:220` already passes it on the main `useProduct`. No fetch change needed; no new exposure to the `allImages` behaviour recorded under SFCC-29. **This is a styling story, not a data story.** | ✅ RESOLVED | — |
42	| 5 | Confluence / Jira | ~~PRD-004 is split and only half is deliverable.~~ **RESOLVED by the ACs.** AC 4 specifies the URL updating *without* full page reload — that is the same-master variant switch, which is this story. SFCC-708 covers *cross-master* related colours with different style codes (products that are not natural variants of one master). The split is clean and the ACs state this story's half explicitly. | ✅ RESOLVED | — |
43	| 4 | Confluence | **PARTLY resolved — I closed this too fast earlier.** AC 1 supersedes PRD-004's wording for the **single-colour** case (`Colour: Bay Blue`, not "Only available in"). But PRD-004's *"Also available in"* applies to the **cross-SKU** case, which is real and still live — just deferred to SFCC-708. Verified 2026-08-31: the product API exposes only `c_careInstructions` and `c_sizeFit`, so no related-colours attribute exists yet, which is why the AC was moved out on 2026-08-12. **Design gap:** the Figma `labelContainer` (`40000307:13867`) holds two text nodes sizing to `"Colour:"` + value — there is no "Also available in" label variant anywhere in the design. | 🟡 CLARIFY → **SFCC-708** | Design needs to specify the group label for the cross-SKU case before SFCC-708 builds it. Not blocking SFCC-91. |
44	| 8 | CODEOWNERS | **Cross-squad, and squad ownership of the PDP is itself contested.** `swatch-group/` → Squad B + tier-2 + tier-1 (`CODEOWNERS:103`, Tier 2). `pages/product-detail/` → Squad B (`CODEOWNERS:162`) — but `.claude/rules/squadA.md:4,34` claims it for Squad A. The ticket is labelled `Squad-A`. | 🟡 CLARIFY | CODEOWNERS is authoritative for review routing; the squadA.md conflict is a separate governance item. |
45	| 9 | Confluence | **Design tracker vs ticket.** 04.72 records PDP components finalised **Aug 13** under an explicit *"once locked, no further design changes are permitted"* rule, yet design was pending on Aug 26. The tracker's PDP scope also never lists a colour swatch. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Raise as process drift; does not block this build now that nodes exist. |
46	
47	---
48	
49	## 🔵 Notes
50	
51	| # | Source | Finding |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| 21 | Figma | **The design's variants do not match the base component's.** `pdp/product-colour-picker` (`40000307:13823`) ships **two sizes × three states**: `Large/Rectangle` (48×72) and `Small/Rounded` (20×24), each in `Unselected` / `Selected` / `Focus`. Base `Swatch` offers `square` \| `circle`. A 48×72 portrait rectangle is not a square and a 20×24 rounded rect is not a circle — so the recipe needs its own variant vocabulary, not the base's. |
54	| 22 | Figma | **No Hover and no Disabled state exist in the design** — and both absences are *correct*. `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` states hover-to-preview is *"a custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live"*; and the AC handles unpopulated variations by **not rendering them**, so no disabled state is needed. The design is internally consistent with the PRD here. |
55	| 23 | Figma | **Placement is fixed.** `Colour Options` sits inside `Content Card and Colour Swatch` at y=126 (218×104), between the product description and the size selector — `40000307:14062`. The PDP content column also carries `Default` / `Warning` / `Unavailable` / `Coming soon` states at desktop **and** mobile. |
56	| 18 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I framed the recipe name as a judgement call. It is not — it is mechanically enforced. `recipeGuards.test.ts:351` sets `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` and its comment reads *"Anything else must be namespaced (e.g. ZimmFooter, not Footer)."* Base SFCC registers a `SwatchGroup` recipe, so a key literally named `SwatchGroup` would deep-merge the base and **fail `npm run test`**. Name it **`ZimmSwatchGroup`**. |
57	| 10 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I reported that base `Swatch` selects on hover at `lg`+ and implied it affects the PDP. It does not. `swatch.jsx:69` applies the hover handlers only when there is no `href` (`{...(href ? {} : selectHandlers)}`), and `use-variation-attributes.js:152-153` sets `href: null` only in *controlled* mode — the quick-view modals. On the PDP path `href` is a real URL, so swatches are `RouteLink`s and hover-select never fires. Live in quick-view modals only. |
58	| 11 | Codebase | Base `disabled` is **visual only** — fed to `useMultiStyleConfig` at `swatch.jsx:35`, never spread onto the `<Button>`; no `isDisabled`, no `aria-disabled`, no click guard. Not triggered by this story's ACs (unpopulated variants are not rendered), but PRD-014's disabled *size* swatch will hit it. |
59	| 15 | Codebase | **Dormant landmine — only if `swatch-group` is overridden.** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:71-72` imports the swatch by base path. The moment an override exists, those must become `'../swatch-group'` / `'../swatch-group/swatch'` or Storybook and Vitest silently exercise the **base** component. The render-slot architecture sidesteps this entirely. |

# SFCC-91 — PreBuild gate (rev 2)

**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
**Depth:** `standard` · **Run date:** 2026-08-31
**Repo state:** `develop` @ `269d5d4`, clean, level with origin
**Scope note:** run as a fresh build. Jhoan's branch and PR #70 deliberately ignored per instruction.

**Rev 2 changes:** Marcel supplied the ACs and 16 Figma node URLs — blockers #1, #2 and #3 are
**resolved**. One **new blocker** surfaced from the PRDs. Two earlier findings were **wrong** and
are corrected below.

---

## Verdict — ✅ CLEAR. All blockers resolved; plan written and handed off.

---

## Resolved since rev 1

| # | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🔴 No acceptance criteria | **Resolved.** Five ACs supplied, covering swatch availability, single-colour text-label fallback, selected indication, selection behaviour, and unpopulated index images. |
| 2 | 🔴 Figma unresolvable | **Resolved — and my diagnosis was wrong.** I reported the files as returning stub pages under a View-seat restriction. That was incorrect: `get_metadata` without a node ID only lists top-level pages, and this file's page list is degenerate. Given node IDs, every node resolves. Access was never the problem. |
| 3 | 🔴 Design missing above 4 colours | **Resolved, and the design answers it concretely.** `40000307:13867` / `40001992:51882` each carry a `Pagination` frame (48×24, `Icon_chevron_left` + `Icon_chevron_right`) in the label row above a fixed 4-swatch window. **The >4 treatment is chevron pagination — not wrap, scroll, or "+N".** Icon dependency satisfied: `ChevronLeftIcon`/`ChevronRightIcon` already exist in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`. |
| 13 | Dependency on SFCC-89 | Confirmed cleared — PR #64 merged 2026-08-27. |

---

## 🔴 The remaining blocker

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | `.docs/prd/` | **Both PRDs say do not build this yet.** `.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 (SPR-26 — Open): *"colour swatch creation and management in Business Manager — map colour attribute values… to hex code or swatch image… Colour mapping exercise TBC. **Do not implement until confirmed.**"* Repeated in `.docs/prd/pdp.md:219` Open Items: *"Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)."* And `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` (PRD-002, confirmed): *"Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names."* The Jira ACs instruct the opposite. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Per AGENTS.md *Doc integrity*: cite the doc, stop, and ask whether the PRD is now stale (SPR-26 resolved by the BM index-image decision) or whether the ticket is running ahead of it. Not a call to make silently. |

---

## 🟡 Clarify / informational

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | AC vs codebase | ~~The AC's swatch source and the base implementation disagree.~~ **RESOLVED — verified against the live dev API 2026-08-31.** `viewType: 'swatch'` exists and is populated. The per-colour swatch group (carrying `variationAttributes: color=[...]`, which is what base `getVariantValueSwatch`'s filter needs) appears **only when `allImages=true`** — and `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:220` already passes it on the main `useProduct`. No fetch change needed; no new exposure to the `allImages` behaviour recorded under SFCC-29. **This is a styling story, not a data story.** | ✅ RESOLVED | — |
| 5 | Confluence / Jira | ~~PRD-004 is split and only half is deliverable.~~ **RESOLVED by the ACs.** AC 4 specifies the URL updating *without* full page reload — that is the same-master variant switch, which is this story. SFCC-708 covers *cross-master* related colours with different style codes (products that are not natural variants of one master). The split is clean and the ACs state this story's half explicitly. | ✅ RESOLVED | — |
| 4 | Confluence | **PARTLY resolved — I closed this too fast earlier.** AC 1 supersedes PRD-004's wording for the **single-colour** case (`Colour: Bay Blue`, not "Only available in"). But PRD-004's *"Also available in"* applies to the **cross-SKU** case, which is real and still live — just deferred to SFCC-708. Verified 2026-08-31: the product API exposes only `c_careInstructions` and `c_sizeFit`, so no related-colours attribute exists yet, which is why the AC was moved out on 2026-08-12. **Design gap:** the Figma `labelContainer` (`40000307:13867`) holds two text nodes sizing to `"Colour:"` + value — there is no "Also available in" label variant anywhere in the design. | 🟡 CLARIFY → **SFCC-708** | Design needs to specify the group label for the cross-SKU case before SFCC-708 builds it. Not blocking SFCC-91. |
| 8 | CODEOWNERS | **Cross-squad, and squad ownership of the PDP is itself contested.** `swatch-group/` → Squad B + tier-2 + tier-1 (`CODEOWNERS:103`, Tier 2). `pages/product-detail/` → Squad B (`CODEOWNERS:162`) — but `.claude/rules/squadA.md:4,34` claims it for Squad A. The ticket is labelled `Squad-A`. | 🟡 CLARIFY | CODEOWNERS is authoritative for review routing; the squadA.md conflict is a separate governance item. |
| 9 | Confluence | **Design tracker vs ticket.** 04.72 records PDP components finalised **Aug 13** under an explicit *"once locked, no further design changes are permitted"* rule, yet design was pending on Aug 26. The tracker's PDP scope also never lists a colour swatch. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Raise as process drift; does not block this build now that nodes exist. |

| # | Source | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | Figma | **The design's variants do not match the base component's.** `pdp/product-colour-picker` (`40000307:13823`) ships **two sizes × three states**: `Large/Rectangle` (48×72) and `Small/Rounded` (20×24), each in `Unselected` / `Selected` / `Focus`. Base `Swatch` offers `square` \| `circle`. A 48×72 portrait rectangle is not a square and a 20×24 rounded rect is not a circle — so the recipe needs its own variant vocabulary, not the base's. |
| 22 | Figma | **No Hover and no Disabled state exist in the design** — and both absences are *correct*. `.docs/prd/pdp.md:17` states hover-to-preview is *"a custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live"*; and the AC handles unpopulated variations by **not rendering them**, so no disabled state is needed. The design is internally consistent with the PRD here. |
| 23 | Figma | **Placement is fixed.** `Colour Options` sits inside `Content Card and Colour Swatch` at y=126 (218×104), between the product description and the size selector — `40000307:14062`. The PDP content column also carries `Default` / `Warning` / `Unavailable` / `Coming soon` states at desktop **and** mobile. |
| 18 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I framed the recipe name as a judgement call. It is not — it is mechanically enforced. `recipeGuards.test.ts:351` sets `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` and its comment reads *"Anything else must be namespaced (e.g. ZimmFooter, not Footer)."* Base SFCC registers a `SwatchGroup` recipe, so a key literally named `SwatchGroup` would deep-merge the base and **fail `npm run test`**. Name it **`ZimmSwatchGroup`**. |
| 10 | Codebase | **CORRECTION to rev 1.** I reported that base `Swatch` selects on hover at `lg`+ and implied it affects the PDP. It does not. `swatch.jsx:69` applies the hover handlers only when there is no `href` (`{...(href ? {} : selectHandlers)}`), and `use-variation-attributes.js:152-153` sets `href: null` only in *controlled* mode — the quick-view modals. On the PDP path `href` is a real URL, so swatches are `RouteLink`s and hover-select never fires. Live in quick-view modals only. |
| 11 | Codebase | Base `disabled` is **visual only** — fed to `useMultiStyleConfig` at `swatch.jsx:35`, never spread onto the `<Button>`; no `isDisabled`, no `aria-disabled`, no click guard. Not triggered by this story's ACs (unpopulated variants are not rendered), but PRD-014's disabled *size* swatch will hit it. |
| 15 | Codebase | **Dormant landmine — only if `swatch-group` is overridden.** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:71-72` imports the swatch by base path. The moment an override exists, those must become `'../swatch-group'` / `'../swatch-group/swatch'` or Storybook and Vitest silently exercise the **base** component. The render-slot architecture sidesteps this entirely. |
| 24 | Codebase | Base recipe `theme/components/project/swatch-group.js` declares `parts: ['swatch','swatchButton']` while its `baseStyle` carries five keys — the exact undeclared-parts defect `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts:101` exists to catch. Declare every part you read. |

| 16 | Codebase | On `develop`; the `PreToolUse` hook blocks writes there. `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` already exists on origin (Jhoan's) — a fresh branch needs a different name. |
| 17 | Docs | `.docs/memory/projectState.md` last updated 2026-08-24; `sprintScope.md` still reads *"Sprint 0 — Foundation"*. Don't scope from either. |

---

## Recommended architecture — a render slot, not a `swatch-group` override

The strongest option, and it dissolves findings #7 and #15 rather than managing them.

Commit `227171e` added `renderHeader?: (props) => React.ReactNode` to the `product-view` override —
a **render slot on the default export**, defaulting to the base behaviour exactly. Its message
argues the case directly:

> *"overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
> wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props the
> default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still requires the
> slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which is a graver
> breach of the faithful-port rule."*

A `renderVariationAttributes` slot is the direct analogue. It means:

- **No `swatch-group` override** → PLP and the recommendations carousels are untouched.
- **No Tier 2 / Squad B file** in the diff, and no cross-squad approval gate.
- **No import-path landmine** (#15) to create and then have to remember.
- A new `ZimmColourSwatch` / `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in `ui-kits/`, following the
  `zimmProduct*` four-file pattern established by PR #64.

The alternative — a faithful `swatch-group` port plus a `ZimmSwatchGroup` recipe — is the
conventional route, but it changes PLP and every carousel, and needs Squad B plus Tier 2 sign-off.

---

  exactly one component `.tsx` does (`footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`), and only inside a
  `__css={{...styles.part, ...conditional}}` spread the recipe cannot express.
- `textStyle` set in the recipe, and it stays a bare key — there is no `var()` substitute for the
  composite expansion.
- Hooks above any early return; `const intl = useIntl()` then `intl.formatMessage(...)` (never
  destructured — `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`).
- Labels via `react-intl`, **not** `useUiCopy` — `useContentful.ts` sends no `locale`, so `uiCopy`
  would serve the space default to all 8 storefronts.
- Two hard gates on `npm run test`: `recipeParts.test.ts:101` (declared parts must cover every
  `styles.*` read) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6 guards, incl. bare-token and namespacing).

**No hook override.** All variation logic funnels through `useDerivedProduct` →
`useVariationAttributes` → `useVariationParams`, and `product-view` already receives decorated
`variationAttributes`. Overriding a hook routes through the `hooks/index.js` barrel, which resolves
in the app build but **not** in Storybook or Vitest.

  to be pulled from the 16 nodes at plan time.
- **No build or test was run.** Every codebase claim is read from source. `audit:tokens` is known

## Audit — plan.md

| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Yes | `9f46912` (+ doc fix `2d8a9a7`) | Verbatim extraction confirmed byte-for-byte by the whole-feature sweep independently |
| 2 | Yes | `ab04241` (+ fix `6631e05`) | 2 rework rounds — wrong token name, then a focus-ring-covered-by-sibling bug found post-commit |
| 3 | Yes | `b16298e` | 4 rework rounds — pagination-selection, a fabricated citation, a stuck focus ring + layout shift, a covered outline + unbounded truncation |
| 4 | Yes | `7139687` | Set/bundle isolation independently re-confirmed via JSX branch analysis, not just diff hunks |

**Whole-feature manifest audit (dispatched fresh, comparing the full `269d5d4..HEAD` diff against plan.md §3, not just per-step):** **IN SCOPE.** All 8 CREATE + 3 MODIFY files match exactly; all 14 excluded paths (`theme/foundation/`, `swatch-group/`, `image-gallery/`, `translations/`, `.storybook/`, `hooks/`, `.claude/rules/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `config/`, `.github/workflows/`, etc.) confirmed untouched across every commit, not just the latest. Every file's tier independently re-derived from `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`/`CODEOWNERS` directly (not trusted from the plan) and matches. All 6 commit messages confirmed attribution-clean.

**Files in the diff not in the manifest:** none. `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages}.md` churn is the only thing outside the literal 11-file list — expected, automatic, not a finding.

## Sweep — internal consistency

- **Import convention** — consistent within the feature and matches pre-existing local precedent (`product-detail/index.tsx`'s own SFCC-89-era `ZimmProductMeta` import uses the identical relative shape). No divergence.
- **Recipe/token/structure conventions** — consistent. `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6) and `recipeParts.test.ts` (14/14) both pass, mechanically confirming namespacing and parts-completeness across both new recipes.
- **🟡 UNIFORM finding — the value `4` (swatches per page) is independently declared five times with no shared source:** `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:13`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:41`, and three more inside `index.test.tsx` (lines 204, 233, 258). Confirmed directly by grep. The `.css.ts` file's own comment admits nothing enforces they match (*"If `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in index.tsx ever changes, update this to match"*). No correctness impact today — all five currently agree — but `overrideStyling.md`'s own co-location section names the exact right fix pattern this codebase already has and didn't use here: a small shared module (like the existing `footerShared.ts` precedent) rather than five independent literals. **This is a real DRY violation a per-step review structurally could not have caught**, since each of the five sites looks completely correct in isolation.
- **🔵 note — JSDoc density gap.** `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` calls `useIntl()` without explaining the `components.md` container/presentational exemption inline, unlike the exemplar (`zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:41-45`, which spells it out in the file itself). The reasoning exists only in the commit message. Cosmetic, not blocking.
- **🔵 note — a commit-sequencing artifact, explained, not a defect.** Commit `6631e05`'s registry snapshot already lists `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, one commit before `b16298e` creates any of its files. Cause: the registry-regeneration hook scans the live filesystem, not git's index — Step 3's molecule was already sitting uncommitted in the working tree (mid-rework, which is how Marcel was able to view it in Storybook) at the moment the atom fix was committed. HEAD's final state is fully correct; this is an artifact of interleaved rework-round sequencing, not corruption.

## Sweep — external conformance

- **Against the exemplar (`zimmProductStyleCode/`, commit `227171e`)** — the four-file pattern and the render-slot precedent are both followed correctly. The one gap (JSDoc density, above) is real but minor.
- **Against `.claude/rules/*`** — held across the whole feature, not just per-file. `overrideStyling.md`'s styling hierarchy, `components.md`'s structure rules, `conventions.md`'s naming/DRY rules all checked directly against both components together; only the magic-number-4 finding surfaced.
- **Figma citations, cross-checked for internal agreement** (no live Figma access this pass) — every place the feature cites a specific design fact (48px width, 2:3 ratio, 8px/4px gaps, the 192px reserved width) agrees with every other citation of the same fact. No internal contradiction found.
- **🟡 should-fix, re-confirmed a third time, independently — the atom's `href`-less branch is a genuinely inoperable ARIA radio.** `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:85-96` renders `role="radio"`/`aria-checked`/a real `tabIndex` on a plain `<span>` with no `onClick`, no `onKeyDown`, and no callback prop anywhere in its type surface for a future caller to wire one in. This whole-feature sweep independently compared against base SFCC's own `swatch.jsx` and confirmed base's real equivalent (a `<Button>`, always) genuinely is operable in the same no-`href` case — ours is not, at all, not even "missing Space" as CodeRabbit's narrower framing put it. Three independent investigations have now found this (Step 2's original build Tester, the local CodeRabbit review, and this sweep) — it has zero live callers today (`product-detail` always supplies `href`), so it's not a shipped regression, but it's real, load-bearing for the exact future use the component's own comment names, and unlike this codebase's other genuinely-incomplete states (e.g. `swatch-group`'s disabled-colour logic), it isn't logged anywhere yet.

## UNIFORM findings (the point of this phase)

1. **Magic number `4` duplicated 5× with no shared source** (this feature, confirmed real, cheap to fix — see recommendation below).
2. **`recipeGuards.test.ts`'s fuzzer blind spot recurred twice in this one feature** (`selected` on the atom, `isPaginated` on the molecule) — both already known from Build's own rounds, re-surfaced here because it's genuinely the same shape hitting twice, not a new finding.
3. **The href-less-atom accessibility gap has now been found three separate times by three separate investigations** — worth logging properly rather than leaving it to be rediscovered a fourth time.
4. **No custom Zimmermann i18n message has ever reached the translation extraction pipeline**, repo-wide (from the CodeRabbit review, already in handoff.md) — the single largest UNIFORM finding of this whole build, and the only one that isn't scoped to this feature at all.

## PR body as written

See the draft below, presented separately for Marcel's review before anything is opened.

## Could not verify

- **Live rendering** — no dev-server/Storybook access in the audit agents; all layout claims corroborated via jsdom assertions and Marcel's own prior manual checks, not reproduced fresh here.
- **AC 4's absence from any test/story name** — the whole-feature Tester (no Jira access) flagged this as unexplained. **Resolved directly, not actually open:** AC 4 (URL updates without full reload) was deliberately never given a dedicated unit test anywhere — it's a browser-level behaviour, already flagged in plan.md as a known, accepted E2E coverage gap, and already verified manually by Marcel at Step 4's visual checkpoint. Not a silently-dropped AC.
- **`generateRegistry.mjs`'s consumer-count semantics** (`ZimmColourSwatch` shows 1, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` shows 3, despite similar file layouts) — pre-existing tooling this feature didn't author; not chased further.
- **Whether the href-less-atom gap's shape recurs elsewhere in `ui-kits/atoms/`** — flagged as a recurrence risk on reasoning, not confirmed via a second instance.

## Recommendation before opening the PR

One real, cheap, non-blocking finding worth a decision: the magic-number-4 duplication. My recommendation is a narrow fix-round back to `zimmerMANNBuild` — extract one shared constant (following the existing `footerShared.ts` cross-file pattern) that `index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, and the three test sites all import, rather than five independent literals. Cheap, mechanical, no design risk. Everything else is either already resolved, already logged as a deliberate follow-up, or genuinely outside this build's scope.

# ZimmColourSwatch (SFCC-91 Step 2/4) — Test Report

Note up front: this environment gave me only `Read` and `Bash` — no sub-agent dispatch tool exists here, so I worked every angle myself sequentially rather than literally fanning out. All commands below were actually executed in this session; outputs are real, not summarized from memory.

---

## 1. Compiles and passes

```
npx tsc --noEmit        → EXIT 0, zero output (matches stated baseline: 0 errors)
npm run lint             → EXIT 1, "20 problems (4 errors, 16 warnings)" — identical to stated
                           pre-existing baseline; the 4 errors are still only at
                           routes.tsx:23,24 and recipeGuards.test.ts:116,335. Nothing in
                           zimmColourSwatch/* appears anywhere in lint output.
npm run test             → EXIT 0, "27 passed (27)" files, "417 passed (417)" tests.
```
The jump from the stated 408→417 (+9, not +8) is explained and confirmed: the new `index.test.tsx` adds 8 tests, and `recipeParts.test.ts` (a `test.each` keyed off every multipart recipe on disk) organically grew by one more generated case now that `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` exists as a second multipart recipe. Ran it standalone with `--reporter=verbose` and confirmed a case literally named `zimmColourSwatch` passed:
```
✓ .../recipeParts.test.ts > multipart recipes declare every part their component reads > zimmColourSwatch
```
CONFIRMED clean, ONE-OFF (nothing to generalize — this angle is fine).

---

## 2. Tokens (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)

```
EXIT 1 — "4 unacknowledged" / "22 acknowledged" — identical to stated baseline, all in
header/index.tsx, header.ts, navConstants.ts. None in this step's files.
```
I didn't just trust the unchanged count — I `git stash -u`'d this step's two changed files and re-ran the audit: **52 files scanned without this step, 54 with it** (exactly +2, matching `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` + `index.tsx`, since `.test.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` are excluded by the script itself). Both new files were genuinely scanned and contributed zero raw-value findings. Stash was popped back cleanly (verified via `git status` + file `md5`).

**However — this angle has a blind spot that matters a lot here (see Angle 3, Finding A).** `audit:tokens` only flags raw hex/px/rem/em literals; it has no concept of validating that a `var(--zimm-*)` string names a real registered variable. A component can reference a completely non-existent token and this script reports it as clean. That's exactly what happened in this step.

---

## 3. Styling conformance

### 🔴 Finding A — `backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-background-02)'` references a CSS custom property that does not exist anywhere in this codebase
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31`

I did not take the recipe's own comment ("Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02']") at face value. I read the **entire** `theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (the sole source `ZimmTokensGlobal` uses to emit the `:root` block — confirmed it's the only `<Global>` in the repo touching `--zimm-*`, the other one being unrelated `@font-face` CSS). The registered background aliases are `--zimm-color-bg-01` through `--zimm-color-bg-07` (line 53–59) — **never** `--zimm-color-background-NN`. A repo-wide grep for `zimm-color-background` returns exactly two hits, both inside this new component's own files (the recipe, and its own test asserting the same wrong string back at itself) — nothing else in the codebase uses or defines this name.

I then proved the real-world effect in an actual Chromium instance (Playwright, already installed locally), not jsdom:

decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

finding names, never stages, never commits.

  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

1	---
2	name: zimmerMANNPreBuild
3	description: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
4	---
5	
6	The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
7	been named.
8	
9	**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
10	yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
11	pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
12	way.
13	
14	**Input:** `$ARGUMENTS` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
15	If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.
16	
17	## Depth
18	
19	Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:
20	
21	| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
24	| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
25	| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |
26	
27	Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
28	`exhaustive` is.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Phase 0 — position
33	
34	Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
35	states current position.
36	
37	Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
38	blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
39	dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Phase 1 — gather
44	
45	Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
46	a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.
47	
48	### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`
49	
50	Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
51	attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
52	decision that contradicts the description.
53	
54	Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
55	no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
56	still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.
57	
58	### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`
59	
60	Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.
61	
62	Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
63	describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
64	that supersedes it.
65	
66	### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`
67	
68	The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
69	Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.
70	
71	Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
72	`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.
73	
74	The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
75	`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
76	is stale.
77

`exhaustive` is.

---

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

- **Never write to the repo's config** — `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,

content.content: --- name: zm-tester description: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash model: sonnet color: yellow --- You test one implemented step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build. **You find problems. You never fix them** — fixing is the Implementer's job, and a tester that fixes its own findings cannot be trusted to report honestly. **Falsify, don't confirm.** Prefer a deletion or a probe to a reading. ## Fan out **Dispatch your own sub-agents, one angle each.** Tell each what the others cover so it stays in its lane, and give each the step's spec and pass criteria. Then reconcile their findings yourself — where two disagree, go to source; do not average them or take the more confident one. ## Re-point the angles for this step The angles below are the standing set, not a fixed checklist. Ask what *this* step's failure mode actually is and spend the budget there. **Drop an angle that has gone vacuous and say you dropped it** — a base-parity check on a Zimmermann-authored file proves nothing. 1. **Compiles and passes.** `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`. Paste real output, not a summary. `recipeGuards.test.ts` is the hard styling gate — a failure there is always a real finding. 2. **Tokens.** `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`. Advisory, not in CI, so read it yourself. Only new unacknowledged findings in touched files are yours to report. 3. **Styling conformance.** Bare Chakra token keys, raw literals in component files, Chakra array shorthand where explicit media queries are required, unnamespaced recipes, recipes missing from `theme/components/index.ts`. 4. **Structure.** Named export matches folder name; props type is `Props`; story present for anything exported from its folder; own test file for anything with real logic; no data-fetching hook in a leaf component (`useIntl` / `useUiCopy` excepted). 5. **Imports.** No base-path import of an already-overridden component — this is the one that passes CI and still ships wrong. No circular imports, no `../../../..` chains deeper than 3, no import from a later-sprint feature. 6. **Accessibility.** Every `` has `alt`; every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; any non-native element with `onClick` has `role`, `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown`. 7. **Against the ticket.** Re-read the ACs. Is each one actually satisfied by what was built? Add an angle when the step earns one. The one worth adding whenever a step changes rendered output: **predict what Marcel will see at the visual checkpoint** — which URL, which viewport, what should be on screen, and what would indicate a defect. Include anything that will look wrong but is correct. ## Evidence bar - Label every finding **CONFIRMED** (you reproduced it) or **PLAUSIBLE** (reasoned but unproven). - Report real observed numbers from real runs, never what a description claims. - **Do not pad.** A short list of real defects beats a long list of speculation. If an angle is clean, say so in one line — the Scorer needs to tell checked-and-clean apart from not-checked. ## Two required sections **What I tried to falsify.** Say what you attacked and how it survived. A clean report with no attempt behind it is not evidence of anything. **What I could not verify.** Name what you could not reach and why. A prior loop on this codebase ran eight invocations before anyone found a real layout-shift defect, because every pass reported only what it *had* checked. If you believe a space is genuinely covered, show your search. ## Reporting One block per angle. Each finding: `file:line`, what's wrong, which rule or AC it violates, 🔴 must-fix / 🟡 should-fix / 🔵 note, **CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE**, and **UNIFORM or ONE-OFF**. UNIFORM means the defect shape could plausibly repeat across the feature's other files. Per-step scoring is structurally blind to that — a pattern applied consistently but wrongly passes every individual review, and one did survive five commits here. Flagging it is how it gets caught early.

content.content:
---
name: zm-scorer
description: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: sonnet
color: red
---

## Two modes

**Build mode (default).** You are the gate on a Zimmermann build loop — score the work against the
six axes below and return PASS or REWORK. Everything in this file describes this mode.

**Findings mode.** `zimmerMANNReview` invokes you to score *claims* rather than work: does each
finding survive scrutiny? Return **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent
with what you read, decisive evidence missing — say what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the
citation does not support the claim — say what is actually true). The six axes do not apply.
Review supplies the full brief; this note exists so the mode is not a surprise to anyone reading
this file.

The rest of this file is **build mode.**

---

You see the plan step, the diff, the Tester's findings and the Orchestrator's scope verdict, and
you decide whether the work is done.

You are independent of the builder and the tester. You are not a cheerleader and you are not a
second tester. Your job is a **judgement**: is this good enough to move on, given what the step
said it would deliver?

## The six axes

| Axis | What PASS looks like |
|---|---|
| **Pass criteria** | Every criterion in the step is met, with evidence — not asserted |
| **Correctness** | `tsc` clean, `npm run test` green, no 🔴 findings from the Tester |
| **Design fidelity** | The rendered output matches the named Figma nodes — variants, states, spacing, tokens |
| **Conformance** | Styling hierarchy, recipe namespacing, structure and import rules all hold |
| **Completeness** | Story and test present where the rules require them; ACs actually satisfied |
| **Restraint** | Nothing built that the step didn't ask for |

**Design fidelity is its own axis and cannot be inferred from green gates.** No automated check on
this stack catches a layout defect: `width: 'xl'` resolved through `theme.sizes`, blew contact
icons to 576px and destroyed the global footer on every page — while passing tsc, eslint, vitest,
CodeRabbit and Storybook a11y. If the visual checkpoint has not happened yet for a step that
changes rendered output, this axis is **UNVERIFIED**, not PASS.

**Restraint takes its evidence from the Orchestrator's verdict.** An OVER or UNDER verdict fails
this axis; you make the judgement, the Orchestrator supplies the finding.

## Verdict

**PASS** — all six hold. **REWORK** — one or more fail.

On REWORK, say exactly which axis, quote the evidence, and give the Implementer a specific
instruction. "Improve quality" is not an instruction; "`footer.css.ts:22` uses `gap: 'xs'` — a bare
token key that fails recipeGuards guard 4; use `var(--zimm-scale-xs)`" is.

Label each finding **CONFIRMED** or **PLAUSIBLE**.

## Two required sections

**What I tried to falsify.** A PASS with no falsification attempt is not a PASS. Say what you
attacked and how the work survived. A verification pass that finds nothing has not been shown to
be capable of finding anything.

**What I could not verify.** Name what you could not reach, and say plainly if an axis is
UNVERIFIED rather than passed.

## Output shape

1. Per-axis table, six rows, most severe first
2. **Overall: PASS or REWORK**
3. What I tried to falsify
4. What I could not verify
5. Each defect: `file:line`, severity, CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE, and the specific instruction
6. If PASS: the single biggest residual risk in shipping this step

## The round cap

Track the round number. **On the third REWORK for the same step, stop the loop** and surface to
Marcel with what has been tried, what is still failing, and your read on why it isn't converging.
Three failed rounds means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not the implementation.

Never soften a verdict to end the loop, and never soften one to be agreeable. A false PASS moves
the defect downstream to CodeRabbit, to Tim, or to production.
===
---
name: zm-implementer
description: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: sonnet
color: green
---

You implement **one step** of an approved Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Not the next step, not
an improvement you noticed on the way — one step.

## Before you write anything

1. Confirm you are **not** on `develop` or `main`. A `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit on those branches; if you are on one, stop and say so rather than working around it.
2. Read the step's file manifest and its pass criteria. Those are your definition of done.

## How you work

- **Only touch files the step names.** If the work genuinely cannot be completed without touching
  a file the plan didn't anticipate, **stop and report it**. Do not decide for yourself.
- **Never stage and never commit.** No `git add`, no `git commit`, no `git checkout`, no `git
  stash`. Leave your changes in the working tree — the skill owns the commit, and it only commits
  a step the Scorer has passed and Marcel has eyeballed.
- **Copy-first is not optional.** Overriding a base SFCC file means: copy it verbatim to the
  mirrored path, convert `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`, replace `PropTypes` with real types
  (no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`), get `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, prove the override renders — and
  **then stop and present before making any functional change.**
- **Import an already-overridden component by relative path**, never by its
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` base path. A base-path import compiles and ships fine but
  silently renders the *unstyled base component* in Storybook and Vitest, because the
  `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real webpack build.
- Follow the styling hierarchy: `textStyle` → `var(--zimm-*)` → theme recipe → `sx` → scoped
  `.scss`. Never a bare Chakra token key. Never a raw hex/px/rem/em in a component file — if a
  value genuinely has no token yet, make it a **named constant** with a comment containing
  `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder` or `audit-allow: <reason>`, never an inline literal.
- Name new recipes `Zimm*` and register them in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- A component exported from its folder needs a story. A component with real logic needs its own
  test file.

## When you finish the step

Run and report the output of:

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
```

`npm run test` includes `recipeGuards.test.ts`, which is the hard styling gate — five guards that
fail the build on bare token keys, unnamespaced recipes, and unregistered recipes. If it fails,
fix it before reporting done; that failure is yours, not the loop's.

Report what you changed, file by file, and the evidence for each pass criterion. Do not claim a
criterion is met without showing what proves it.

#### UNIFORM-1 — Tester gap: DRY violations within a single step are not in any angle

The zm-tester for Step 3 ran across 7 angles and caught real defects (pagination/selection, fabricated citation, truncation coverage). It did NOT flag `const SWATCHES_PER_PAGE = 4` in `index.tsx:13` and `const PAGE_SIZE = 4` in `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:41` — two files in the same step defining the same magic number independently, where the css.ts file's own comment explicitly warned they must be kept in sync manually. This was caught only by PostBuild's whole-feature internal-consistency sweep, 1 build round later.

**Attribution: TESTER** — the brief's 7 angles have no "same value typed twice in multiple files of this step" check. The closest is angle 4 (Structure) which covers naming/export/story/test but not intra-step value duplication.

Evidence: `zm-tester agent-a7409054ef415d5fe.jsonl` — final report covers angles 1-7 exhaustively but has no DRY/duplicate-value check; `handoff.md` UNIFORM findings: "the value `4` (swatches per page) is independently declared five times with no shared source"; `postbuild.md` sweep internal consistency: UNIFORM finding.

Disposition: **PROPOSED** — add angle to zm-tester brief.

---

#### UNIFORM-2 — Tester gap: no angle for React state/logic correctness beyond "compiles and passes"

The functional updater issue (CR#3: `handlePrevPage`/`handleNextPage` reading raw `pageStart` via functional updater instead of clamped `currentPageStart`) was not caught by the Step 3 Tester, though the Tester ran extensive pagination tests. The Tester correctly caught the pagination/selection defect (initial-mount landing on wrong page), but both defects involve pagination state management. The functional updater issue only surfaces when `populated.length` shrinks while the component is mounted — a scenario none of the Tester's fixtures exercised. The 7 standing angles are: (1) compiles/passes, (2) tokens, (3) styling, (4) structure, (5) imports, (6) accessibility, (7) against-the-ticket. None is "React logic correctness: state management, closures, derived-vs-raw state reads."

**Attribution: TESTER** — absent angle, not a checker that failed to find something.

Evidence: `agent-a7409054ef415d5fe.jsonl` — "Pagination mechanics: real render+click tests confirmed all of..." — tests with static fixtures only; CodeRabbit CR#3 (`zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:148-149`) found `handlePrevPage`/`handleNextPage` use unclamped `pageStart` in functional updater; fixed in `54e924f`.

Disposition: **PROPOSED** — add angle to zm-tester brief.

---

#### UNIFORM-3 — Plan gap: interactive-element disabled states not required in Figma nodes for molecule steps

The disabled chevron visual color (`stroke: var(--alias-color-icon-disabled, #D1D1D1)`) was not in the Step 3 plan, not in the Step 3 pass criteria, not checked by the Tester, and not caught by PostBuild's sweep. Marcel spotted it manually after PostBuild completed and the PR was opened as a draft. This required its own investigation round (Tier 1 token addition to `colour.ts` + `zimmTokens.ts`), a mid-PostBuild return to Build, and an additional commit.

The root cause: the plan's Step 3 visual checkpoint specified layout Figma nodes (`40001992:51881`, `40000307:13867`) for measuring dimensions, but never asked "what does the disabled state of the pagination button look like?" PreBuild's Figma guidance explicitly lists disabled as a required state to check ("every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled"), but that instruction was not converted into a plan-level pass criterion for the pagination controls.

**Attribution: PLAN** — the zm-planner did not carry PreBuild's "check all states" instruction through to Step 3's concrete Figma node list and pass criteria.

Evidence: `plan.md` Step 3 visual checkpoint column: `40001992:51881 / 40000307:13867 Type=Large (Squared) 192×104 — label row 24px, swatch row 72px, Pagination right-aligned at x=144` — no disabled-state node. `plan.md` decisions table row 5: "pagination ships in Step 3 — disabled at the ends" — functional disabled but no visual treatment. The session transcript confirms Marcel's discovery: "observed missed implementation, chevron-disabled for the paginated colour swatches: [6 Figma URLs]" posted after PostBuild Phase 5.

Disposition: **PROPOSED** — add explicit pass-criteria instruction to zm-planner brief.

---

#### CITATION-1 — Build skill: `cr review --uncommitted` is wrong after commits

`zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md:123` says `cr review --uncommitted` in the expensive pre-handoff gates. `--uncommitted` reviews only staged changes and tracked edits — once every step has been committed (which is the precondition for this gate: "run the expensive gates once" after "every step has passed"), there are no uncommitted changes, so the command reviews nothing. The correct command for a full feature branch review against develop is `cr review --light --base develop`, which is what was actually used in SFCC-91 (`handoff.md`: "cr review --light --base develop | 4 findings").

Disposition: **PROPOSED** — one-line fix in Build skill.

`zimmerMANNPreBuild/SKILL.md:89-90` says "Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: PR #59 (component + CSS layer, focused vs shared recipes) and PR #56 (the token layer)." PR #59 (100 files, global footer) is the right reference for shared global-chrome components and co-located recipe patterns. Evidence: `plan.md` Step 3 visual checkpoint column: `40001992:51881 / 40000307:13867 Type=Large (Squared) 192×104 — label row 24px, swatch row 72px, Pagination right-aligned at x=144` — no disabled-state node. `plan.md` decisions table row 5: "pagination ships in Step 3 — disabled at the ends" — functional disabled but no visual treatment. #### CITATION-1 — Build skill: `cr review --uncommitted` is wrong after commits

`zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md:123` says `cr review --uncommitted` in the expensive pre-handoff gates. `--uncommitted` reviews only staged changes and tracked edits — once every step has been committed (which is the precondition for this gate: "run the expensive gates once" after "every step has passed"), there are no uncommitted changes, so the command reviews nothing. `zimmerMANNPreBuild/SKILL.md:89-90` says "Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: PR #59 (component + CSS layer, focused vs shared recipes) and PR #56 (the token layer)." Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. 4 tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash 5 model: sonnet 6 color: yellow 7 --- 8 9 You test one implemented step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build. **You find problems. You never fix 10 them** — fixing is the Implementer's job, and a tester that fixes its own findings cannot be 11 trusted to report honestly. 12 13 **Falsify, don't confirm.** Prefer a deletion or a probe to a reading. 14 15 ## Fan out 16 17 **Dispatch your own sub-agents, one angle each.** Tell each what the others cover so it stays in 18 its lane, and give each the step's spec and pass criteria. Then reconcile their findings yourself — 19 where two disagree, go to source; do not average them or take the more confident one. 20 21 ## Re-point the angles for this step 22 23 The angles below are the standing set, not a fixed checklist. Ask what *this* step's failure mode 24 actually is and spend the budget there. **Drop an angle that has gone vacuous and say you dropped 25 it** — a base-parity check on a Zimmermann-authored file proves nothing. 26 27 1. **Compiles and passes.** `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`. Paste real output, not a summary. 28 `recipeGuards.test.ts` is the hard styling gate — a failure there is always a real finding. 29 2. **Tokens.** `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`. Advisory, not in CI, so read it yourself. 30 Only new unacknowledged findings in touched files are yours to report. 31 3. **Styling conformance.** Bare Chakra token keys, raw literals in component files, Chakra array 32 shorthand where explicit media queries are required, unnamespaced recipes, recipes missing 33 from `theme/components/index.ts`. 34 4. **Structure.** Named export matches folder name; props type is `Props`; story 35 present for anything exported from its folder; own test file for anything with real logic; 36 no data-fetching hook in a leaf component (`useIntl` / `useUiCopy` excepted). 37 5. **Imports.** No base-path import of an already-overridden component — this is the one that 38 passes CI and still ships wrong. No circular imports, no `../../../..` chains deeper than 3, 39 no import from a later-sprint feature. 40 6. **Accessibility.** Every `` has `alt`; every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; any non-native 41 element with `onClick` has `role`, `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown`. 42 7. **Against the ticket.** Re-read the ACs. Is each one actually satisfied by what was built? 43 44 Add an angle when the step earns one. The one worth adding whenever a step changes rendered 45 output: **predict what Marcel will see at the visual checkpoint** — which URL, which viewport, 46 what should be on screen, and what would indicate a defect. Include anything that will look wrong 47 but is correct. 48 49 ## Evidence bar 50 51 - Label every finding **CONFIRMED** (you reproduced it) or **PLAUSIBLE** (reasoned but unproven). 52 - Report real observed numbers from real runs, never what a description claims. 53 - **Do not pad.** A short list of real defects beats a long list of speculation. If an angle is 54 clean, say so in one line — the Scorer needs to tell checked-and-clean apart from not-checked. 55 56 ## Two required sections 57 58 **What I tried to falsify.** Say what you attacked and how it survived. A clean report with no 59 attempt behind it is not evidence of anything. 60 61 **What I could not verify.** Name what you could not reach and why. A prior loop on this codebase 62 ran eight invocations before anyone found a real layout-shift defect, because every pass reported 63 only what it *had* checked. If you believe a space is genuinely covered, show your search. 64 65 ## Reporting 66 67 One block per angle. Each finding: `file:line`, what's wrong, which rule or AC it violates, 68 🔴 must-fix / 🟡 should-fix / 🔵 note, **CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE**, and **UNIFORM or ONE-OFF**. 69 70 UNIFORM means the defect shape could plausibly repeat across the feature's other files. Per-step 71 scoring is structurally blind to that — a pattern applied consistently but wrongly passes every 72 individual review, and one did survive five commits here. Flagging it is how it gets caught early. 73

You never fix them** — fixing is the Implementer's job, and a tester that fixes its own findings cannot be trusted to report honestly. **Falsify, don't confirm.** Prefer a deletion or a probe to a reading. ## Fan out **Dispatch your own sub-agents, one angle each.** Tell each what the others cover so it stays in its lane, and give each the step's spec and pass criteria. Then reconcile their findings yourself — where two disagree, go to source; do not average them or take the more confident one. ## Re-point the angles for this step The angles below are the standing set, not a fixed checklist. Ask what *this* step's failure mode actually is and spend the budget there. **Drop an angle that has gone vacuous and say you dropped it** — a base-parity check on a Zimmermann-authored file proves nothing. 1. **Compiles and passes.** `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`. Paste real output, not a summary. `recipeGuards.test.ts` is the hard styling gate — a failure there is always a real finding. 2. **Tokens.** `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`. Advisory, not in CI, so read it yourself. Only new unacknowledged findings in touched files are yours to report. 3. **Styling conformance.** Bare Chakra token keys, raw literals in component files, Chakra array shorthand where explicit media queries are required, unnamespaced recipes, recipes missing from `theme/components/index.ts`. 4. **Structure.** Named export matches folder name; props type is `Props`; story present for anything exported from its folder; own test file for anything with real logic; no data-fetching hook in a leaf component (`useIntl` / `useUiCopy` excepted). 5. **Imports.** No base-path import of an already-overridden component — this is the one that passes CI and still ships wrong. No circular imports, no `../../../..` chains deeper than 3, no import from a later-sprint feature. 6. **Accessibility.** Every `` has `alt`; every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; any non-native element with `onClick` has `role`, `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown`. 7. **Against the ticket.** Re-read the ACs. Is each one actually satisfied by what was built? 8. **Intra-step DRY.** For every named constant or literal value that appears in more than one file of this step's output, confirm there is a single shared source — not parallel literals that a comment says to keep in sync. Check the component file, its .css.ts recipe, and its test file. A value typed three times with no shared source is a UNIFORM finding even when all three currently agree. If an angle is clean, say so in one line — the Scorer needs to tell checked-and-clean apart from not-checked. ## Two required sections **What I tried to falsify.** Say what you attacked and how it survived. A clean report with no attempt behind it is not evidence of anything. **What I could not verify.** Name what you could not reach and why. UNIFORM means the defect shape could plausibly repeat across the feature's other files. ---
name: zm-planner
description: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch
model: opus
color: purple
---

You are the planner for Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. You run on Opus at high effort because
planning is the step where a wrong call is most expensive — everything downstream inherits it.

You are given evidence already gathered from Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase
and Figma. **You do not gather more evidence unless a specific gap blocks the plan.** You turn
evidence into a sequence someone can execute.

## What you produce

A plan with these parts, in this order:

1. **Goal statement.** One paragraph, in this shape:
   > Build <story> as prescribed by <TICKET>, as designed in <Figma node>, as approached by the
   > FED handbook, as established in <exemplar PR>, using the token / component / CSS / override
   > approach as appropriate.

2. **Scale call — commits or branches, and how much machinery.** State it and justify it; do
   not leave it implicit for each agent to infer.
   - Single branch, multiple commits: one coherent feature, one reviewer, < ~10 files.
   - Multiple branches: independent surfaces, different squads, or a Tier 2 file that needs a
     separate approver. Name the split.
   - **Then say how much loop the work actually warrants**, and defend it. Scale to the need —
     nothing too crazy, no overthinking. A two-point story does not get the full loop, and
     over-scaled machinery is a defect in the plan, not thoroughness. If you are dropping a
     step or an angle because the work is small, say which and why.

3. **File manifest.** Every file to create or modify, with its tier and owner. Tier comes from
   `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, never from `.claude/registry/*.md`
   (its Tier column is a derived heuristic and is wrong in places). Mark any Tier 1 file as
   **BLOCKED** unless the user has named it explicitly and confirmed owner approval.

4. **Steps.** Each step is one commit's worth of work, with:
   - what changes
   - **pass criteria** — concrete and checkable, not "works correctly"
   - which existing skill to call for it, if any

5. **Loop configuration.** For each step, what the Tester should check and what the Scorer
   treats as PASS. Be specific to this story, not generic.

6. **Open questions.** Anything you could not resolve. These block the handoff.

## Rules you plan against

These are the Zimmermann build rules that most often get planned around incorrectly:

- **Override vs custom:** does a file exist at the mirrored path under
  `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`? Yes → override it, copy-first (copy verbatim,
  convert to TS, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, prove it renders, **then stop and present** before any
  functional change). No → new custom component under `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/`.
  Note `.docs/architecture.md:130` still says `components/custom/` — that directory has never
  existed. Do not plan into it.
- **Styling hierarchy:** `textStyle` → `var(--zimm-*)` → theme recipe → `sx` → scoped `.scss`.
  Never a bare Chakra token string (`color="text.default"`), never a raw hex/px/rem/em in a
  component file.
- **Focused vs shared style:** used by one component → co-located `<name>.css.ts`. Needed by two
  or more split-out files of the same feature → a shared module in `theme/components/`
  (`footerShared.ts` is the reference). Never copy the same literal into two files.
- **New recipes are namespaced `Zimm*`** and registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
  An unnamespaced recipe silently deep-merges with the SFCC base recipe of the same name.
- **Responsive steps are explicit media queries** off the shared `BP` breakpoints, never Chakra's
  array shorthand — the array form fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`.
- **Components take data as props.** No data-fetching hooks in leaf components; `useIntl` and
  `useUiCopy` are the only documented exceptions.
- **A story is required** for anything exported from its folder. A component with real logic gets
  its own test file even when a parent's `play` covers the same ground.

## What you must not do

- Do not write or edit any file. You produce a plan; the Implementer executes it.
- Do not plan any change to `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**` or `.docs/prd/**`. They are Tier 1 Governance and out of scope.
- Do not infer squad ownership from `squadA.md` / `squadB.md` — they contradict each other on
  PDP/PLP and are both drafts. Read `CODEOWNERS` instead.
- Do not invent an acceptance criterion the ticket does not contain. If an AC is missing, that is
  an open question, not something for you to fill in.

content.text:
The flag correction is agreed. The question is whether to add `--light` or run full mode. The options for `cr review` are:

- `cr review --base develop` — full review against develop (all changed files, no depth limit)
- `cr review --light --base develop` — faster/cheaper; CodeRabbit caps the review depth and may skip lower-confidence findings
- `cr review --base develop --files <glob>` — full review scoped to a subset of files (useful when only specific paths matter)

The pre-handoff gate is the one shot before the PR goes public — it's exactly where you want full coverage, not the lighter pass. My recommendation is `cr review --base develop` (full, no `--light`). The tradeoff is it takes longer and costs more tokens per run, but this gate only fires once per feature.

questions.question: Which CodeRabbit command for the pre-handoff gate?

---
name: zimmerMANNBuild
description: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
---

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `$ARGUMENTS` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --uncommitted             # CodeRabbit locally, before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".
